issues.description: The verification patch rewrites the existing CPUID imports, calls, and adjacent executable comments to use a different wrapper instead of specifying the original core intrinsics at the centralized external boundary.
issues.rationale: The base functions call `core::arch::x86_64::{__cpuid, __cpuid_count}` and carry their original comments. This reviewed revision inserts new explanatory/rustdoc text, replaces the imports with `x86::cpuid::native_cpuid::cpuid_count`, and replaces all four intrinsic calls, even though the PR's purpose is to add specifications. The CHANGES_REQUESTED review says not to modify executable comments, asks whether the two original functions can be added to verified_libs, and flags the added comment. The next commit does exactly that: it adds external specifications for `__cpuid` and `__cpuid_count` under `verified_libs/vstd_extra/src/external/x86.rs`, restores the original imports/calls/comments, and leaves only `#[verus_spec]` contracts at the OSTD caller. This is one `preserve-exec-code` root cause, with `centralize-trusted-boundaries` providing the correct location for the external intrinsic contracts.
issues.verification: source-only; historical Verus not executed. Inspected the force-pushed original review commit, its fixing successor, current head, full live remote discussion, and fixed before/after source.
